Names banks, vendors, amounts and signed contracts (e.g. first PPP contract signed).

brief: Montenegro's media channel for tender and contract intelligence splits into three tiers: a small set of open, directly-confirmed local publishers that actually carry procurement detail (Bankar.me for banking-sector specificity, Investitor.me for central-bank equipment tenders, Dan for aggregate procurement-accountability numbers, and MANS as the NGO watchdog whose documents feed the press), a set of flagship dailies the cell brief names (Vijesti, Pobjeda, CdM, RTCG) that my searches never surfaced directly and which must be verified by live fetch before being trusted, and a layer of paywalled aggregators and regional/English outlets (eKapija, Tenderi Live, SeeNews, Bloomberg Adria, montenegrobusiness.eu) useful for corroboration but not for unlicensed automated collection. The clearest confirmed signal patterns are cancelled and legally challenged tenders — Montenegro was reported as the Western Balkans record-holder for annulled procedures, and a worked ANPR software case shows the discriminatory-documentation complaint template — plus institutional payment-infrastructure milestones (CBCG instant payments, EPC licence, treasury equipment tender) that precede procurement. Notably, no media report of a Montenegrin commercial bank procuring an information system was found in local-language search, which supports the cell's premise that private-bank contracts surface only obliquely and suggests future queries should target vendor-side and signing-ceremony language rather than tender vocabulary. The largest remaining gaps are regional ICT/fintech trade press, the banks' own press and tender pages, and Cyrillic-script querying, none of which this run reached before the search budget ran out.
